newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Lenzing says to cut jobs, costs.
newsitem.headline: Lenzing says to cut jobs, costs.

text.p: Austrian fibre maker Lenzing said on Monday it planned to cut 500 jobs and save 500 to 600 million schillings annually over the next two to three years to cope with structural changes in the industry.

"Long-term structural changes in the European textile industry -- twinned with overcapacity in Asia -- have led to extremely difficult market conditions for the global textile industry," Lenzing said in a statement.
Most of the savings would come from organisational changes that would not require significant investment, Lenzing said. The firm also saw potential to reduce energy, material and financial costs.
Production capacity would be unaffected, it added.
Details of the programme would be finalised in mid-December.
Lenzing said it would enter negotiations with the workforce immediately and forecast natural wastage would account for some of the proposed job losses.
"This forward-looking programme should ensure Lenzing's long-term success," the statement concluded.

In the first half of 1996 Lenzing posted a group pre-tax loss of 84.5 million schillings after a profit of 160 million last year. The firm has said it expects to remain in the red in the second half. -- Janet McBride, Vienna Newsroom 43-1-531 12 254
